games.title: Medical Microbiology Q&A Guide: quick quiz
games.blurb: Quiz for Year 2 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: Which of the following Gram‑positive cocci is most commonly associated with endocarditis in intravenous drug users?
questions.explanation: S. aureus is the leading cause of infective endocarditis in IV drug users.

questions.q: What is the most sensitive rapid diagnostic test for detecting Mycobacterium tuberculosis in sputum?
questions.explanation: NAATs (e.g., Xpert MTB/RIF) detect TB DNA with high sensitivity and provide rapid results.

questions.q: Which virulence factor of Pseudomonas aeruginosa contributes to its resistance to many antibiotics?
questions.explanation: Alginate biofilm formation protects P. aeruginosa from antibiotics and host defenses.

questions.q: A 45‑year‑old patient presents with a painless ulcer on the genitalia. Which organism is most likely responsible?
questions.explanation: Syphilis caused by T. pallidum presents with a painless chancre.

questions.q: Which of the following is the preferred empirical therapy for community‑acquired pneumonia in a patient with no comorbidities?
questions.explanation: Amoxicillin covers Streptococcus pneumoniae, the most common cause of CAP in healthy adults.

questions.q: What is the mechanism of action of vancomycin against Gram‑positive bacteria?
options: Inhibits protein synthesis at the 50S ribosomal subunit
questions.explanation: Vancomycin binds D‑alanine‑D‑alanine termini, preventing peptidoglycan cross‑linking.

questions.q: Which of the following organisms is most likely to cause a urinary tract infection in a catheterised patient?
questions.explanation: P. aeruginosa is a common nosocomial pathogen in catheter‑associated UTIs.

questions.q: Which laboratory test is most useful for diagnosing a fungal infection in a neutropenic patient?
questions.explanation: Serum β‑D‑glucan is a sensitive marker for invasive fungal infections in neutropenic patients.

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of Mycobacterium leprae?
options: Acid‑fast bacillus with a slow growth rate
questions.explanation: M. leprae is cholesterol‑dependent and cannot be cultured in vitro.

questions.q: What is the most common cause of bacterial meningitis in adults in the United States?
questions.explanation: S. pneumoniae remains the leading cause of bacterial meningitis in adults.

games.title: Occupational and environmental lung diseases 2019-2: quick quiz
games.blurb: Quiz for Year 4 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: Which occupational exposure is most strongly associated with silicosis?
questions.explanation: Glass manufacturing involves high levels of crystalline silica dust, making it the classic occupational exposure for silicosis.

questions.q: A 45‑year‑old construction worker presents with progressive dyspnea and a fine inspiratory crackle. HRCT shows reticular opacities predominantly in the upper lobes. Which diagnosis is most likely?
questions.explanation: Upper‑lobe reticular opacities with a history of silica exposure point to silicosis.

questions.q: Which of the following is the best initial screening test for early detection of occupational lung disease in a worker exposed to asbestos?
questions.explanation: Chest X‑ray is the first‑line screening tool for asbestos‑related lung disease.

questions.q: A patient with a history of long‑term exposure to diesel exhaust develops cough and sputum production. Which lung disease is most likely?
questions.explanation: Diesel exhaust is a known irritant that can cause chronic bronchitis.

questions.q: Which occupational exposure is most commonly linked to the development of chronic beryllium disease?
questions.explanation: Beryllium alloy manufacturing exposes workers to beryllium dust, causing chronic beryllium disease.

questions.q: A 60‑year‑old farmer presents with progressive dyspnea, dry cough, and clubbing. HRCT shows diffuse ground‑glass opacities. Which environmental agent is most likely responsible?
questions.explanation: Organic dust exposure from moldy hay can cause farmer’s lung, an allergic alveolitis.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a typical feature of asbestosis on high‑resolution CT?
questions.explanation: Asbestosis typically shows lower‑lobe subpleural fibrosis and honeycombing; upper‑lobe predominance is not characteristic.

questions.q: A 35‑year‑old electrician reports wheezing and dyspnea after prolonged exposure to welding fumes. Which lung condition is most likely?
questions.explanation: Welding fumes can cause bronchiolitis obliterans, a small‑airway disease.

questions.q: Which occupational exposure is most strongly associated with the development of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis?
questions.explanation: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis has no known occupational cause; other exposures are linked to specific pneumoconioses.

questions.q: A 50‑year‑old worker exposed to high levels of organic solvents presents with cough, dyspnea, and diffuse interstitial infiltrates on chest X‑ray. Which diagnosis is most likely?
questions.explanation: Organic solvent exposure can lead to diffuse interstitial lung disease.

games.title: Cough: case showdown
games.blurb: Case Showdown for Year 4 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: A 68‑year‑old man presents with a productive cough that has worsened over the past 3 weeks. He has a history of chronic bronchitis and is a heavy smoker. Chest auscultation reveals coarse crackles at the bases. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The combination of a chronic productive cough, coarse crackles, and a long‑standing smoking history is most characteristic of a COPD exacerbation.

questions.q: A 45‑year‑old woman reports a dry cough that started 2 days ago after a cold. She has no fever, no sputum, and her chest X‑ray is normal. What is the next best step in management?
questions.explanation: A viral upper‑respiratory infection is the most likely cause of a short‑duration dry cough; supportive care is adequate.

questions.q: A 22‑year‑old college student presents with a non‑productive cough that has persisted for 6 weeks. He reports nocturnal cough and a mild fever. Physical exam is unremarkable. Which investigation is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: A persistent cough lasting >4 weeks warrants a chest X‑ray to exclude pneumonia, tuberculosis, or other structural disease.

questions.q: A 55‑year‑old man with a history of asthma presents with a dry cough that worsens at night. His peak expiratory flow is 40% of predicted. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Nighttime cough and markedly reduced peak expiratory flow are classic for an asthma exacerbation.

questions.q: A 30‑year‑old woman presents with a chronic dry cough that started after a recent upper respiratory infection. She has a history of gastro‑oesophageal reflux disease (GERD). What is the most likely cause of her cough?
questions.explanation: GERD is a well‑known trigger of chronic dry cough, especially when it follows an upper respiratory infection.

questions.q: A 70‑year‑old man with a history of smoking presents with a productive cough and weight loss. Chest X‑ray shows a right upper lobe infiltrate. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: In a heavy smoker with weight loss and an upper‑lobe infiltrate, lung cancer is a strong consideration and should be ruled out before attributing the findings to pneumonia.

questions.q: A 35‑year‑old woman presents with a dry cough that started 3 weeks ago. She has no fever, no sputum, and her chest X‑ray is normal. She reports a history of seasonal allergies. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Seasonal allergies and a dry cough with a normal chest X‑ray point toward upper airway cough syndrome (post‑nasal drip).

questions.q: A 60‑year‑old man presents with a productive cough and dyspnoea. He has a history of chronic bronchitis and is on long‑term oxygen therapy. Physical exam reveals digital clubbing. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Digital clubbing in a chronic smoker with a productive cough is most consistent with bronchiectasis.

games.title: Population and Demography: drug duel
games.blurb: Drug Duel for Year 2 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: Which drug is most commonly used to reduce mortality in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease by inhibiting the synthesis of low‑density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol?
questions.explanation: Atorvastatin is a statin that inhibits HMG‑CoA reductase, lowering LDL cholesterol and reducing cardiovascular mortality.

questions.q: Which medication is the first‑line treatment for type 2 diabetes in patients with a BMI >30 kg/m² and a history of heart failure?
questions.explanation: SGLT2 inhibitors improve glycaemic control and reduce heart failure risk in obese patients with type 2 diabetes.

questions.q: A 65‑year‑old man with chronic kidney disease stage 3 is started on a drug that reduces proteinuria by inhibiting the renin‑angiotensin system. Which drug is most likely prescribed?
questions.explanation: Lisinopril, an ACE inhibitor, reduces proteinuria and slows CKD progression.

questions.q: Which of the following drugs is associated with a characteristic side effect of a red‑tinged urine due to inhibition of the renal tubular secretion of a fluorescent dye?
questions.explanation: Rifampicin causes red‑orange urine by inducing hepatic enzymes that metabolise the dye.

questions.q: Which drug is the preferred first‑line therapy for hypertension in a patient with a history of stroke and diabetes?
questions.explanation: Losartan, an ARB, is preferred in stroke and diabetes due to renal protection and lower risk of hypoglycaemia.

questions.q: A 55‑year‑old woman with newly diagnosed rheumatoid arthritis is started on a disease‑modifying antirheumatic drug that inhibits tumour necrosis factor‑α. Which drug is most likely?
questions.explanation: Etanercept is a TNF‑α inhibitor used as a biologic DMARD in rheumatoid arthritis.

questions.q: Which medication is most commonly prescribed for the prevention of venous thromboembolism in patients undergoing major orthopedic surgery and is a reversible factor Xa inhibitor?
questions.explanation: Rivaroxaban is a direct oral factor Xa inhibitor used for VTE prophylaxis after orthopedic surgery.

questions.q: A 70‑year‑old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is started on a long‑acting bronchodilator that is a muscarinic antagonist. Which drug is most likely?
questions.explanation: Tiotropium is a long‑acting antimuscarinic bronchodilator used in COPD management.

games.title: Pharmacology Wk 1 & 2: drug duel
games.blurb: Drug Duel for Year 3 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: Which drug is a selective COX‑2 inhibitor used primarily for osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis, and is associated with an increased risk of myocardial infarction at high doses?
questions.explanation: Celecoxib selectively inhibits COX‑2 and has a higher cardiovascular risk profile at high doses.

questions.q: What is the primary mechanism of action of the antiepileptic drug levetiracetam?
questions.explanation: Levetiracetam binds to SV2A, modulating neurotransmitter release.

questions.q: Which drug, a first‑generation antihistamine, is most likely to cause anticholinergic side effects such as dry mouth and blurred vision?
questions.explanation: Diphenhydramine is a first‑generation H1 blocker with significant anticholinergic activity.

questions.q: A patient is prescribed a drug that blocks the H2 receptors on gastric parietal cells. Which of the following is the most common adverse effect?
questions.explanation: H2 receptor antagonists are generally well tolerated; the most common adverse effect is mild gastrointestinal upset, including diarrhea.

questions.q: Which of the following drugs is a selective beta‑1 adrenergic antagonist used in hypertension and heart failure?
questions.explanation: Metoprolol is a cardioselective β1 blocker.

questions.q: Which drug is a proton pump inhibitor that irreversibly inhibits the H+/K+ ATPase in parietal cells?
questions.explanation: Omeprazole irreversibly blocks the gastric proton pump.

questions.q: A patient on a drug that inhibits the CYP3A4 enzyme experiences increased plasma levels of a co‑administered statin. Which drug is most likely responsible?
questions.explanation: Ketoconazole is a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor, raising statin levels.

questions.q: Which of the following is the main indication for the drug clopidogrel?
questions.explanation: Clopidogrel is an antiplatelet used in acute coronary syndrome.
